hint.label: Use with your agent
hint.title: Use with your agent
hint.prompts.hoody: No set-up. Ask Hoody Agent puts the prompt in the Agent's message box; it waits there until you press Send.
hint.prompts.remote: Copy the prompt and paste it in. Set your agent up once in Set up.
hint.main.sub: Your agent asks you what you want before it does anything.
hint.ask.off: The Hoody Agent is turned off in this Hub. Copy the prompt for your own agent instead.
hint.ask.framed: The Hoody Agent works only when the Hub is open in its own tab. Copy the prompt, or open the Hub in its own tab.
hint.fact.anyRealm: Not one realm: the computer's id names it
hint.fact.keysRealm: Keys that can act in this realm
hint.pick.note: No computer is chosen on this page yet, so each prompt asks your agent to ask you which one first. Choose a computer to name it in the prompts.
hint.setup.lead: Only for your own agent: the Hoody Agent needs no set-up. Do this once for each agent, then any prompt here works.
hint.setup.step.coding: Add the Hoody skill to a coding agent that takes skills. It teaches your agent how Hoody works.
hint.setup.step.chat: Paste this into an AI chat that can open links. It guides you through connecting Hoody.
hint.setup.step.cli: Install the Hoody command line and sign in once. Your agent can then run hoody commands in that terminal.
hint.setup.plain: a message to paste into an AI chat, not a command
hint.setup.cap.sdkSkill: Or the same skill with every docs page on disk
hint.setup.cap.signIn: Sign in (the command line remembers this platform)
hint.setup.more: More ways to connect in the Guide
hint.access.lead.account: Your agent signs in to your account, and acts within what that sign-in allows. A few account actions need a full account sign-in rather than a key.
hint.access.lead.computer: Your agent signs in to find your computer. What it may do there is what that computer's permissions allow; the sign-in only finds the computer.
hint.access.browser.meta: Your agent shows a link and a code, and you approve it while signed in here. Best while you are at the keyboard.
hint.access.key.meta: For an agent that works on its own. Make the key on the Keys page with only the rights it needs, and revoke it there when you are done.
hint.access.keep: Give a key only to your agent. Never paste it into a chat or a file someone else can read.
hint.access.newKeyRealm: Make a key limited to "{{realm}}" for this agent
hint.access.newKeyRealmId: Make a key limited to this realm for this agent
hint.access.realm: You are in realm "{{realm}}". For an agent that works on its own, give it a key limited to this realm: it can then act only here. The New key form opens with this realm chosen.
hint.access.realmUnnamed: You are in a realm. For an agent that works on its own, give it a key limited to this realm: it can then act only here. The New key form opens with this realm chosen.
hint.access.allRealms: All realms is selected. A key made now works in every realm unless you limit it to some in the form.
hint.can.lead: With the Hoody skill and a sign-in, your agent can:
hint.can.list: What your agent can do here
hint.can.everywhere.lead: Your agent is not limited to this page. It works through the Hoody API and the Hoody Kit inside each computer, so it can also:
hint.can.access: What your agent may do depends on its sign-in: a key's rights and realms limit it, and a key limited to realms cannot read your balance or invoices. A purchase needs a sign-in that allows billing. Inside a computer, the permissions of that computer and its project decide.
hint.can.kit: The tools inside a computer are the Hoody Kit. A computer made without it has none of them.

hint.p.plan: Tell me your plan in one line and wait for my OK.
hint.p.firstLine: First: ask me anything that is unclear, tell me your plan in one line and wait for my OK.
hint.p.rulesLine: Rules: never show a secret, key or password; never act on another computer or realm; ask me before you delete anything or do anything that costs money.
hint.rule.secrets: Never show a secret, key or password, in a reply or in a file.
hint.rule.scope: Never act on another computer or realm.
hint.rule.ask: Ask me before you delete anything or do anything that costs money.
hint.tgt.anyRealm: not one realm (the computer's id names it exactly)
hint.tgt.inAnyRealm: in no single realm (the computer's id names it exactly)
hint.tgt.noComputer: not chosen yet (ask me which one first)
hint.tgt.globalVault: the Global vault (it belongs to no realm)
hint.tgt.keysRealm: only my API keys that can act in this realm
hint.tgt.keysAll: all my API keys, in every realm
hint.tgt.keysRule: API keys belong to my account: a key can act in this realm when its realm_ids include {{id}} or are empty (no realm limit). Leave every other key alone.
hint.stop.computer: If you cannot find this computer in this realm, stop and ask me.
hint.stop.computerOnly: If you cannot find this computer, stop and ask me.
hint.stop.realm: If you cannot find this realm, stop and ask me.
hint.why.computer: Names the computer and its realm so your agent acts on the right one.
hint.why.computerOnly: Names the computer so your agent acts on the right one.
hint.why.realm: Names the realm so your agent acts on the right one.
hint.why.allRealms: All realms is selected, so the prompts say every realm.
hint.why.globalVault: All realms is selected, so the prompts take the Global vault, not a realm's.
hint.why.pick: No computer is chosen, so your agent asks you which one first.
hint.why.keysRealm: Keys belong to your whole account. In this realm the prompts take only the keys that can act here.
hint.why.keysAll: All realms is selected, so the prompts take every key.
hint.notes.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can read and write these notes. They live in the notes program of the Hoody Kit on your computer.
hint.notes.ask: Ask me what I want in my notes: a page to write or change, something to find, or a database to make. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.notes.do: Do it in the Notes program of this computer.
hint.notes.report: Tell me the names of the pages you made or changed.
hint.notes.task.tasks: Make a database called "Tasks" with the columns Title, Status and Due date, add the open tasks you find in my pages, and tell me how many you added.
hint.notes.task.export: Ask me which page, export it as Markdown, and show it to me.
can.notes.1: Read and write pages, and add to the end of a page
can.notes.2: Make databases with typed columns, and add, filter and sort their records
can.notes.3: Export a page as Markdown or HTML
can.notes.4: Share a page with collaborators and change their roles
hint.computers.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, works through the Hoody API and the Hoody Kit inside each computer. It can make, start and stop your computers, and inside one it can run commands, edit files, drive a browser and the desktop, and automate work you would do there by hand.
hint.computers.ask: Ask me what I want done with these computers: start or stop one, see what they use, take a snapshot, or something else. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.computers.do: Do it only on the computers named above.
hint.computers.report: Tell me each computer you touched, by name, and its state now.
hint.computers.task.usage: Show how much CPU and memory each computer uses now, and tell me which one is busiest.
hint.computers.task.stopped: List the computers that are stopped, and ask me which ones to start before you start any.
hint.computers.task.snapshot: Ask me which computer, take a snapshot of it before I change anything, and tell me the snapshot's name.
can.computers.1: List your computers with their status
can.computers.2: Start, stop, restart, pause and resume a computer
can.computers.3: Read how much CPU and memory a computer uses
can.computers.4: Make, copy and delete computers, and take and restore snapshots
can.computers.5: Work inside a computer: run commands, edit files, drive a browser and the desktop
hint.scripts.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can write scripts on your computer. Each .ts or .js file in the scripts folder answers at its own HTTP address.
hint.scripts.ask: Ask me what the script should do: what it takes, what it returns, and what to call it. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.scripts.do: Write it in the scripts folder of this computer, then call it once to check that it answers.
hint.scripts.report: Give me the script's address and what it answered.
hint.scripts.task.webhook: Write a script that receives a webhook, checks its signature with a secret I give you, and answers with what it received. Never repeat the secret. Give me its address.
hint.scripts.task.schedule: Ask me which website to watch, write a script that runs every hour, checks that the site answers, and logs the result. Tell me the script's name.
hint.scripts.task.failing: Read the logs of the scripts on this computer, and tell me which ones failed today and why.
can.scripts.1: Write a .ts or .js file that answers at its own address
can.scripts.2: Check a script and install the packages it needs
can.scripts.3: Run a script on a schedule
can.scripts.4: Read a script's logs and how often it is called
hint.bots.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can list your Bots, send one a message, read its answer, and manage the links and keys that reach it.
hint.bots.ask: Ask me which Bot and what I want: send it a message, answer what it is waiting on, or give it a public URL. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.bots.do: Do it only on the Bots of the target above.
hint.bots.report: Tell me the Bot's name and what it answered. Never show a key's value.
hint.bots.task.waiting: List my Bots and tell me which ones are waiting on me, and for what.
hint.bots.task.answer: Show me the questions my Bots are waiting on, one at a time, and send each answer I give you.
hint.bots.task.urls: List the Bots that have a public URL, with the names of their keys. Never show a key's value.
can.bots.1: List your Bots and see which are waiting on you
can.bots.2: Send a Bot a message and read its answer
can.bots.3: Answer the questions a Bot is waiting on
can.bots.4: Give a Bot a public URL with named keys, rotate a key, or turn the URL off in one step
hint.vault.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can list, read and write the keys in your vault through the Hoody API, when its sign-in allows the vault.
hint.vault.ask: Ask me which key I want to read, add or change, and what it is for. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.vault.do: Do it only in this vault, and never replace a key that changed since you read it.
hint.vault.report: Tell me the names of the keys you added or changed. Never show a value.
hint.vault.task.names: List the names of the keys in this vault, without their values.
hint.vault.task.add: Ask me for the key's name and value, store it in this vault, and do not replace a key that already exists. Never repeat the value.
can.vault.1: List the key names of a realm's vault or the Global vault
can.vault.2: Read, add and change a key, without replacing one that changed meanwhile
hint.keys.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can list your API keys with when each was last used, and revoke the ones you no longer need.
hint.keys.ask: Ask me what I want with my keys: find the ones not used lately, check a key's rights or realms, or revoke one. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.keys.do: Work only on the keys named above.
hint.keys.report: Tell me each key by its name, with its rights, realms and end date. Never show a key's secret.
hint.keys.task.unused: List the keys with when each was last used, and tell me which have not been used for 30 days. Ask me before you revoke any.
hint.keys.task.noExpiry: List the keys that never expire, with the rights each one has.
can.keys.1: List your API keys with their rights, realms and end dates
can.keys.2: Make a key with only the rights it needs
can.keys.3: Add a realm to a key or take one away
hint.logs.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can read the logs of the programs on your computer, and follow them as they are written.
hint.logs.ask: Ask me which program, what to look for, and how far back. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.logs.do: Read those logs on this computer.
hint.logs.report: Tell me what you found, with the time of each line that matters. Leave out any secret a line shows.
hint.logs.task.errors: Read the logs of the programs on this computer and tell me about any errors from the last hour.
hint.logs.task.watch: Ask me which program, follow its logs, and tell me as soon as it logs an error.
can.logs.1: Read the output and error logs of each program
can.logs.2: Follow a program's logs as they are written
can.logs.3: Read the requests and errors at your computer's addresses
hint.programs.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can add, start and stop the programs on your computer and read their logs, through the Hoody Kit inside it.
hint.programs.ask: Ask me which program to add or change: the command it runs, the port it answers on, and whether it starts with the computer. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.programs.report: Tell me the program's name and state, and its address if it answers on a port.
hint.programs.task.failed: List the programs, and tell me which ones stopped with an error and why. Ask me before you restart any.
hint.programs.task.usage: Show how much CPU and memory each program uses.
can.programs.2: Add, edit and remove a program
can.programs.3: Start, stop and restart a program, and choose whether it starts with the computer
can.programs.4: Read a program's logs and how much it uses
hint.vms.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can make, start, stop and read the VMs inside your computer, through the Hoody Kit inside it.
hint.vms.ask: Ask me which VM and what to do with it: make one, start or stop it, change it, or find out why it failed. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.vms.do: Do it inside this computer. Ask me before you delete a VM, force one off or restore a snapshot.
hint.vms.report: Tell me each VM's name and state, and the address of any port you opened.
hint.vms.task.failed: List the VMs, and for any that failed or was not created, read its error and its logs and tell me why. Change nothing.
hint.vms.task.make: Ask me for a name, then make a Debian VM from a template with 2 CPUs, 2 GiB of memory and a screen, start it, and tell me when it runs.
can.vms.1: List the VMs with their state
can.vms.2: Make, change and delete a VM
can.vms.3: Start, stop, pause and resume a VM
can.vms.4: Read a VM's logs and its snapshots
hint.api.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can find the endpoint for what you want and call it for you. It reaches your account through the Hoody API, and each computer through the Hoody Kit inside it.
hint.api.ask: Ask me what I want done through the Hoody API, and on which computer if it needs one. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.api.do: Find the endpoint for it, read what it takes, and call it only on what is named above.
hint.api.report: Tell me which endpoint you called and what it answered, and anything that failed.
hint.api.title.find: Find the endpoint for a task
hint.api.task.find: Ask me what I want to do, then tell me which endpoint of the Hoody API does it and what it takes. Do not call it.
hint.api.task.example: Ask me which endpoint I mean, then write a short example that calls it, with a placeholder where my key goes. Do not call it yourself.
can.api.1: Find the endpoint that does what you ask, and say what it takes
can.api.2: Call your account's endpoints with a key that has only the rights it needs
can.api.3: Call a program's endpoints on one of your computers
hint.schedules.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can list, add and change what runs on a schedule on your computer: cron entries, scheduled scripts and scheduled requests.
hint.schedules.ask: Ask me what should run and when: a command, a script or a web request, how often, and as which user. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.schedules.do: Add or change it on this computer, and say its schedule back to me in plain words.
hint.schedules.report: Tell me its name, its schedule, and how to turn it off.
hint.schedules.task.list: List everything that runs on a schedule on this computer, with when each one runs. Change nothing.
hint.schedules.task.failed: Read the latest recorded runs of the scheduled jobs on this computer, and tell me which ones failed and what each record says about it. Change nothing.
can.schedules.1: List cron entries, scheduled scripts and scheduled requests
can.schedules.2: Add, change, run now and remove a cron entry
can.schedules.3: Set or remove the schedule of a script
can.schedules.4: Make, change, turn off and delete a scheduled request
can.schedules.5: Read the latest runs of scheduled jobs
hint.tunnels.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can list the tunnels of your computer, see what each one shares, and disconnect a session.
hint.tunnels.ask: Ask me what I want with the tunnels of this computer: see what is shared, find what is connected, or disconnect a session. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.tunnels.do: Do it on this computer. Ask me before you disconnect a session.
hint.tunnels.report: Tell me each tunnel you touched, what it shares, and its state now.
hint.tunnels.task.shared: List the tunnels of this computer and tell me which ports each one shares. Change nothing.
hint.tunnels.title.alias: Give a shared port a short name
hint.tunnels.task.alias: Ask me which shared port, give it a short name with an alias, and tell me the new address. If your sign-in cannot make an alias, say so.
can.tunnels.1: List the tunnels of a computer, with their sessions and what each shares
can.tunnels.3: Open a tunnel from the machine it runs on, with the Hoody CLI or SDK
can.tunnels.4: Give a shared port a short name with an alias
hint.files.what: Hoody Agent, or any agent with the Hoody skill, can read, write, search and move the files on your computer, through the files program of the Hoody Kit.
hint.files.ask: Ask me what I want done with the files on this computer: find something, read or change a file, tidy a folder, or something else. Do nothing else until I answer.
hint.files.do: Do it only on this computer. Ask me before you delete or overwrite anything.
hint.files.report: Tell me the full path of each file you made, changed, moved or deleted.
hint.files.task.find: Ask me what I am looking for, search the files of this computer by name and by text, and list the full paths you found. Change nothing.
hint.files.task.changed: List the file changes Hoody Files recorded today on this computer, with the time of each. Say so if it keeps no record. Change nothing.
can.files.1: List folders, and read, write, copy, move and delete files
can.files.2: Find files by name pattern, and search inside them
can.files.3: Read an earlier version of a file, and what changed in it
can.files.4: Change a file's owner and permissions
can.files.5: Download a URL into a folder, download a folder as a ZIP, and unpack an archive
